top.text: Loom's library from Mobbin is the strongest library example, with search, folders and recording details.
Zoom from Mobbin shows the richest permission-edit sequence in these screenshots, including an expiration option.
Vimeo from Mobbin separates named collaborators and roles from link privacy.
Grain from Mobbin has the clearest sequence from transcript text to a timestamped comment.
Loom from Mobbin shows editable AI chapters that connect directly to Elevate's chapter work.
SchoolAI from Mobbin takes outcomes and learner insights through to a successful CSV download.
Kajabi from Mobbin shows a clear hierarchy from course to learner to lesson progress.
Coursera from Mobbin shows learner assessment results with both the overall grade and its parts.

legend: ✓ = screenshots show clear evidence for a meaningful part of the question; partial = nearby or incomplete evidence; ✗ = not shown in this report, not a claim that the product lacks it. Ratings use all kept screenshots, including ones that also answer other questions. Q1 to Q3 cover recordings; Q4 to Q6 cover reporting. None of the Q2 screenshots prove automatic learner-own-only access.

differences.text: Loom and Zoom solve different retrieval needs: Loom supports finding items across a library, while Zoom keeps several recording files attached to one meeting. Essentials needs both course-wide search and an event bundle.
Vimeo separates privacy from collaborator rights; Zoom adds optional time limits and passcode controls. This is richer than treating "share" as only copying a link.
Grain ties discussion to transcript times; Loom makes AI chapter structure editable. Together they support reviewing a precise simulation moment and correcting generated navigation.

Circle emphasises course completion, Kajabi reveals the lesson-level detail beneath a learner's percentage, and SchoolAI clearly labels outcomes and mastery. These measures answer different instructor questions and should keep their labels.

Mixpanel makes group comparisons readable with visible definitions and filters. Coursera makes a learner's grade readable by showing the weight and result of each part. Neither should be squeezed into a single "progress" number.

SchoolAI's download ends with a short success message; Circle's export confirms email delivery. The report screen should say where the file will arrive, rather than leaving instructors to search for it.

practices.text: Use a searchable recording library and keep the session's related files together. Add event, learner and scenario filters as an Essentials-specific extension.
Show the effective audience beside sharing actions. For sensitive debriefs, use explicit named or group access and optional expiry; check the learner-own-only policy separately.
Keep timed transcript, chapters and discussion close to playback. Allow corrections to AI structure and provide a no-transcript screen that still lets people review the video.
Provide course overview, learner detail and export in a consistent reporting context. The full path is built from several examples, not one observed journey.
Label completion, assessed score, mastery and engagement separately; keep metric definitions and comparison filters. Do not use video views or retained users as a mastery score.
Give learners a compact progress view with a path to assessment detail. This idea is supported by Coursera alone; this report does not claim other learner portals work the same way.

open.text: When several learners share a simulation, does "own recording" mean the whole event, a clip for each participant, or a release the instructor approves? Zoom groups recordings by meeting and Vimeo gives access by name, but neither answers this.

Should feedback, transcript, comments and downloads follow the video audience, and what happens at semester end? Zoom shows these settings, but the screenshots do not show how they depend on each other.

Who approves AI chapter labels and timed feedback before learners see them, and how should these link to the competencies defined in module 03? Loom and Grain show that AI chapters can be edited, not that they are valid for assessment.

To compare groups fairly, where does attendance come from, how are retries handled, and how are different scenario or rubric versions made comparable? SchoolAI labels mastery and Mixpanel shows comparison controls; neither screenshot defines Elevate's assessment rules.

For the Learner Portal and Canvas, which system's grade, recording link and competency result counts, when is it synced, and how are regraded results matched up? Coursera's personal grades and SchoolAI's export show useful end results, but no Canvas connection. Delivery belongs to module 09.

limitations: We kept 37 examples across 10 products from Mobbin and Refero, including seven screen sequences of up to eight screens each. The screenshots were collected earlier; we did not check the products live. Numbered screen sequences keep the library's order and may skip steps in between. We searched web and iOS screens and left out results that did not fit. The screenshots do not show Canvas or Moodle gradebooks, default attendance, recordings that only their own learner can open, or a Canvas connection. The 'Example of what not to do' label marks a risky share setting, a failed AI screen or a measure that should not be copied, not an overall product ranking. No example is marked as shortlisted yet; that happens in a later review.
